The only note on the verse is a hebrew_gloss on 'towns' (Hebrew daughters), which is unrelated to this lemma; no textual_variant note is mapped here. Base fallback (qere) carries the projection.

The of before Ahlab continues an English the inhabitants of that the ASV supplies and then gaps; no morpheme licenses it (rule 30). Rule 33 places a supplied of on a nominal standing with no preposition and no object marker on it, and this name carries אֵת, so that rule does not reach it; its subtraction test decides the same way, since dropping the word leaves Ahlab with the direct-object relation the Hebrew actually gives it and what has gone is a head noun the Hebrew never wrote. None of rule 16's four families covers an of written for a gapped construct head, so the marker does not take it either. The competing readings, which give the word to the name under rule 33 or to the marker under rule 16, are named here under rule 8.

review_notes: Corrected: the five ofs before Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik and Rehob had been given to those place names under rule 33. That rule reaches a nominal standing with no preposition and no object marker on it, and each of these names carries אֵת, so its condition is unmet; its own subtraction test also fails, since dropping the of leaves each name with exactly the direct-object relation the Hebrew gives it and what has gone is the head noun the ASV supplied for the earlier members and then gapped. Each of is now its own `added` unit and each marker remains `unrepresented`.
The first two members keep their ofs on the written recta of יֹשְׁבֵי עַכּוֹ and יֹשְׁבֵי צִידוֹן under rule 19; only the members where the participle is gapped are affected.

The competing reading gives the word to the marker on the analogy of rule 16's demoted-role-phrase family; that was rejected because the of does not state the object relation but the relation to a head noun the Hebrew never writes, so none of rule 16's four families reaches it.
Partition after correction: all 25 source and 28 target IDs are used exactly once.
